title: Site Directed Mutagenesis by PCR
author: Tobias von der Haar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.igucbww

steps.title: Design Mutagenesis Primers
steps.instruction: Design four specific primers for the mutation site.

substeps.instruction: Primer 1: Anneals upstream of the region to be mutated.
Primer 2: Anneals downstream of the region to be mutated in reverse direction, with a 6 nt mismatch to the target at its 3'-end.
Primer M: Anneals to the mutation site, containing the mutation and 15 nt on either side.

steps.title: Perform First Round PCR
steps.instruction: Conduct two separate PCR reactions using the template DNA and a proof-reading polymerase that does not append 'A' overhangs.

substeps.instruction: Note: If using Taq polymerase, the nucleotide before the primer annealing site for Primer M must be a T to allow base-pairing with Taq-appended A residues.

steps.title: Purify First Round PCR Products
steps.instruction: Clean up the DNA from the first round of PCR.

substeps.instruction: Resolve PCR products on an agarose gel.
Retrieve DNA using a gel extraction kit.

steps.title: Perform Second Round PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify the mutated sequence using the products from the first round as templates.

substeps.instruction: Use ~1 μl of each of the two PCR products from round 1 as template.

steps.title: Clone Final PCR Product
steps.instruction: Use the final PCR product for cloning following standard PCR product cloning procedures.
